For translated quotations, separately check that the same meaning and distinctive voice are expressed in idiomatic target-language speech. Identify a concrete obstruction to that reading, not merely a preferred synonym; clarify an implicit referent only where the supplied context settles it. General editorial and mechanical review are outside this comparison. Distinguish source-support findings from translation findings. Write the complete claim accounting and findings to the report path, ending with completion status and any unresolved findings. Reply in at most 150 words with completion status and the report path. Where you cannot write that file, say in your reply that the file could not be written and why, and give the complete report there instead, ending it the same way; the 150-word limit does not apply to that reply.

Use the Harness's native completion/wait mechanism to await the checker's completion and returned reply. Never start a shell or background task that polls for the report path: the file may be absent until you save the reply yourself. Where the Harness has no usable completion mechanism, name that comparison obstacle and follow the incomplete-comparison procedure below.

After checker completion, consume the report by whichever route the Harness allows, without waiting for the other route. Where the checker could not write its file, its reply carries the report instead: save that text to the report path yourself and read it from there. What settles a comparison is the report and not its route, and what settles the report is its last lines: the task has every report end with its completion status and any unresolved findings, so a report carrying that ending is complete by either route and one lacking it is partial by either route, however far its accounting appears to reach. A comparison cut off before it finished leaves accounting that reads as whole, and only the stated completion status tells the two apart. A checker that completes without a complete report leaves an incomplete comparison; a missing or partial report, interruption, timeout or transport failure follows that same procedure, never a further wait for a file. None makes unchecked prose checked.

Read the complete report and validate its claim accounting as well as its findings, after either comparison. Verify that the complete draft is covered and that every pairing sets the draft passage, in its actual contextual meaning and with its qualifications, beside the source passage it rests on, even when the report lists no findings. A faulty pairing does not by itself make the draft faulty. First establish what the draft actually asserts in its full context, then whether the supplied material supports that proposition with its subject, scope and qualifications intact. A merely conceivable stronger reading does not establish a defect. Distinguish a report that has not established its allegation from genuine material ambiguity or unresolved support in the draft. Reject a finding only with exact draft and source evidence showing support or a concrete mismatch in the report’s reading. For a translation finding, use the resolved composition and quotation guidance to establish the target-language reading. Confidence, preferred wording or qualifications present only in the source settle neither kind of finding. Never go looking for outside legitimation of a standpoint already identified as somebody’s own: research answers a relevant, answerable and bounded question of evidence, and scattered examples of people saying a thing establish no “everybody”. Record detected accounting mismatches and each finding’s disposition and evidence beside the report.

Make only supported repairs, preserving the rest of the draft. If the first comparison leads to any change or disputed part of the report, give a fresh checker the complete current draft and original material for one further comparison under the same task. Supply neither the earlier findings nor your defence. There are at most two comparisons, and validate a second report by the same standard. The final comparison is the last one this run completed, whether that is the second or the first: a comparison that did not complete is no comparison at all, so where a further one fails and the prose is exactly what the earlier complete comparison read, that earlier one is final, while prose repaired since has been read by no complete comparison. After it, change no prose at all, not even into a repair the checker itself proposed: a repair no comparison has read is unchecked prose however safe it looks, and what is delivered is the prose the final comparison read.

Where a complete comparison of the current prose leaves no accepted defect and no genuinely unresolved material claim, proceed. Where the final comparison leaves either, deliver the prose exactly as that comparison read it and report every remaining finding beside the draft: the draft passage, the concrete problem, what the supplied material carries instead, and the smallest repair the checker proposed where it proposed one. A remaining finding is what the comparison alleges and the editor settles, so report it as that and never as an established fact about the text. The account says the draft is delivered with known defects before it says anything else about the draft, and it asserts no fidelity for the passages it names. A rejected finding is the writer’s evidenced decision, not the checker’s approval.

Report the findings beside the text rather than in it: in the delivery account, and not inside the draft or the file at the Output Target, because what is written there is prose a later Skill reads as the text. Where the user asks for the findings marked in the document itself, do that instead: the prose stays exactly as the final comparison read it, and each marking is plainly editorial and separable from it, so nothing carries on as publishable prose. Where that document goes to a path, it also carries the same accounting once, as one clearly editorial block, so what the editor has to act on does not exist only in this reply.

Stopping is for prose no comparison has read. A comparison that could not finish, material that could not be supplied in full, and a missing or partial report are each no completed comparison, whichever route it arrived by. Where that leaves the current prose with no complete comparison of its own, nothing is delivered: report the concrete obstacle and say what was and was not compared. Where an earlier comparison completed and the prose is exactly what it read, because a disputed report alone sent an unchanged draft on, that comparison is the final one: deliver the draft as it read the prose, report every remaining finding beside it, and say in the account which comparison did not finish and what it therefore left uncompared. Nothing unread is ever delivered, and a comparison that failed over its own route or its own material is no reason to withhold prose already compared in full.

A stop never destroys the draft. Preserve the current prose where the user can still reach it once this session is over. Where the Output Target is a path, write the prose to a distinct path beside that target whose name cannot be mistaken for the requested artifact, leave the Output Target itself unwritten, and report that path with the comparison status; where the Output Target is the response, carry the complete current prose in the reply, marked as not source-checked, and carried the way `$LIBRARY/references/delivery.md` says a response carries a text. Say which comparisons ran and what remains, so the work can be resumed rather than written again, and never present preserved prose as checked or delivered.

After the final comparison, preserve the compared prose exactly; only the resolved Handoff Metadata and delivery wrapper remain to add. Read the report before removing its scratch directory, and carry whatever a remaining finding needs in order to be understood and acted on into the delivery account first. Only genuine scratch is removed on any exit: the draft and that accounting are not scratch. The report itself is internal working material, not an extra user deliverable.

Keep every necessary wait helper bounded and owned by this run, and retain the identities of the checker and any helpers you start. On completion, failure, timeout, cancellation or interruption, stop outstanding run-owned waiters and delegated work before removing scratch. Verify their terminal state through the Harness or process/task state so they cannot write into scratch after cleanup. Do not terminate unrelated processes or another run's checker. If stopping or verification fails, preserve the draft and needed accounting, retain scratch still reachable by active work, and report cleanup failure with the outstanding identities and obstacle; never claim the run left nothing. Report cleanup failure alongside the comparison and delivery status, without turning unchecked prose into checked prose.

Av Thomas Barregren

Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter. Tidigare sparades felanmälningar som kom per telefon och per mejl var för sig. I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam logg i två av husen. Testet har sammanfattats i en intern anteckning, men om loggen ska användas i fler hus är ännu inte bestämt.

## Statusvisningen prövades före valet

Maya Lind är arbetsledare i underhållsteamet och har svarat på frågor via mejl. Hon beskriver vad teamet ville uppnå:

– Vi ville att kvällspasset skulle se vad morgonpasset redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra, Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.

Innan teamet valde Svale Systems testade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje enskild reparation.

## Telefonen fanns kvar för de boende

Under testet kunde de boende fortfarande felanmäla per telefon. Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen. Testet pågick i åtta veckor.

Om arbetet med kategorierna skriver Maya Lind:

– Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan nästa hus sätter i gång.

## Anteckningen tillskriver inte loggen den kortare tiden

Enligt Elm Quays interna testanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, fördes 31 felanmälningar in i loggen. Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före testet ingår inte i anteckningen.

Under testet var mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning två arbetsdagar, jämfört med tre under de åtta veckorna innan. Perioderna hade olika arbetsbelastning, och anteckningen avstår uttryckligen från att koppla skillnaden till programvaran. Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller hur lång tid reparationerna tog att slutföra.

## Maya Lind ser tillbaka på testet

Hennes bedömning gäller testet som helhet:

– Jag skulle välja att göra testet igen. Att ha en samlad bild av anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka till förberedelserna.

Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger hon inte.

## Större reparationer avgör fortsättningen

Testet har ännu inte utvidgats till fler hus. Underhållsteamet fattar sitt beslut när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer. Den som förbereder ett liknande införande kan läsa [checklistan för införandet](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist). Kundberättelsen publiceras av Svale Systems.

## Claims

Every claim is supported by the text or its material, with exact attribution and proportionate strength. Preserve the state of knowledge: what is unknown or unclaimed is not thereby known not to have happened. Keep uncertainty where it exists and certainty where it is warranted. So does an evaluative characterisation: calling a count high, low or modest needs a comparison, target, capacity or speaker assessment. Otherwise give the count with its exclusions, without that assessment.

This boundary holds in the title, summary, headings and body alike. Preserve chronology, scope and qualifications wherever a claim appears.

# Quoting speech

Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.

Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.

When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.

## What may be repaired

The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

1	# Case-study brief and source
2	
3	SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.
4	
5	## Brief
6	
7	Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.
8	
9	## Material
10	
11	Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.
12	
13	The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.
14	
15	Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:
16	
17	- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
18	- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
19	- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”
20	
21	Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.
22	
23	## Forbidden inferences / judging
24	
25	No claim that software caused the shorter assignment time, saved money, delighted residents or rescued a helpless customer. Do not turn assignment time into completion time. The customer's reservation must survive. Judge whether quotations contribute experience beyond the surrounding narrative, whether supplier narration stays in third person and whether the suggested link accurately describes its destination.
26

1	# Samlad bild av felanmälningarna hjälper Elm Quay
2	
3	Underhållsteamet på Elm Quay Housing prövade i åtta veckor en gemensam reparationslogg från Svale Systems i två hus. Arbetsledaren Maya Lind berättar vad teamet ville uppnå, vad siffrorna från testet visar och inte visar, och vilken del av förberedelserna hon skulle ge mer tid.
4	
5	Av Thomas Barregren
6	
7	Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter. Tidigare sparades felanmälningar som kom per telefon och per mejl var för sig. I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två av husen. Loggen i testet kom från Svale Systems, och om den ska användas i fler hus är ännu inte bestämt.
8	
9	## Statusvisningen prövades före valet
10	
11	Maya Lind är arbetsledare i underhållsteamet och har svarat på frågor via mejl. Hon beskriver vad teamet ville uppnå:
12	
13	– Vi ville att kvällspasset skulle se vad morgonpasset redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra, Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.
14	
15	Innan teamet valde Svale testade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje enskild reparation.
16	
17	## Svale satte upp loggen och utbildade personalen
18	
19	Testet pågick i åtta veckor, och de boende kunde fortfarande felanmäla per telefon. Leverantören konfigurerade loggen och höll två utbildningstillfällen för sex medarbetare.
20	
21	Om arbetet med kategorierna skriver Maya Lind:
22	
23	– Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan nästa hus startar.
24	
25	## Anteckningen tillskriver inte loggen den kortare tiden
26	
27	Enligt Elm Quays interna testanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, fördes 31 felanmälningar in i loggen. Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före testet ingår inte i anteckningen.
28	
29	Under testet var mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning två arbetsdagar, jämfört med tre under de åtta veckorna innan. Perioderna hade olika arbetsbelastning, och anteckningen avstår uttryckligen från att koppla skillnaden till programvaran. Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller hur lång tid reparationerna tog att slutföra.
30	
31	## Maya Lind ser tillbaka på testet
32	
33	Hennes omdöme är inte en slutsats ur siffrorna utan hennes egen bedömning:
34	
35	– Jag skulle välja att göra testet igen. Att ha en samlad bild av anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle lägga in en extra vecka för förberedelser.
36	
37	Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger hon inte.
38	
39	## Större reparationer avgör fortsättningen
40	
41	Testet har ännu inte utvidgats till fler hus. Underhållsteamet fattar sitt beslut när det har kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer. Den som förbereder ett liknande införande kan läsa [checklistan för införandet](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist). Kundberättelsen publiceras av Svale Systems.

"""
# Quoting speech

Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.

Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.

When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.

## What may be repaired

The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

# Source-support report 1: Elm Quay case (sv)

I compared the whole draft with the source: title, lede, headings, body, the three quotations and the closing. The byline was left out as instructed. Seven source-support findings are open and none has been applied to the draft: F1, F2, F5 and F7 are substantive, while F3, F4 and F6 are minor. There are no translation findings and no editorial questions.

## A. Claim accounting

For each draft passage: the source passage it rests on, then whether they differ.

1. **Title "Samlad bild av felanmälningarna hjälper Elm Quay"**
   - Source: "Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation."
   - Differs: the source has Lind's own assessment; the title makes it an unattributed statement by the publisher. "us" becomes "Elm Quay". **F1.**
2. **"Underhållsteamet … prövade i åtta veckor en gemensam reparationslogg från Svale Systems i två hus."**
   - Source: "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "It chose Svale Systems".
   - Supported.
3. **Lede: "Maya Lind berättar vad teamet ville uppnå, vad siffrorna från testet visar och inte visar"**
   - Source: the figures come from "Elm Quay's internal trial note"; "Her final quotation … is not an inference from the figures."
   - Differs: the account of the figures is attributed to Lind. **F2.**
4. **Lede: "vilken del av förberedelserna hon skulle ge mer tid"**
   - Source: "I would set that time aside before the next building starts."; "I would leave an extra week for preparation."
   - Differs: two separate remarks are welded into one claim. **F3.**
5. **"förvaltar 640 lägenheter"**
   - Source: "manages 640 flats".
   - Supported.
6. **"felanmälningar som kom per telefon och per mejl var för sig"**
   - Source: "telephone reports and emails were stored separately".
   - Differs: "emails" is narrowed to fault reports sent by email. **F4.**
7. **"I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva … i två av husen"**
   - Source: the matching sentence.
   - Supported. The report-to-assignment context shows that "felanmälan" and "repair report" name the same thing.
8. **"om den ska användas i fler hus är ännu inte bestämt"**
   - Source: "has not yet expanded; the team will decide after …".
   - Supported.
9. **Heading "Statusvisningen prövades före valet" and the body sentence under it**
   - Source: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair."
   - Supported. No test result is asserted and no supplier comparison is claimed.
10. **"arbetsledare i underhållsteamet … svarat på frågor via mejl"**
    - Source: "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; "All interviews occurred by email".
    - Supported.
11. **"Hon beskriver vad teamet ville uppnå" and quotation 1**
    - Source: "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information."
    - Supported.
12. **Heading "… utbildade personalen"**
    - Source: "trained six staff".
    - Differs: six staff becomes the whole staff. **F5.**
13. **"Testet pågick i åtta veckor, och de boende kunde fortfarande felanmäla per telefon."**
    - Source: "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "kept telephone reporting open for residents".
    - Supported.
14. **"Leverantören konfigurerade loggen och höll två utbildningstillfällen för sex medarbetare."**
    - Supported.
15. **"skriver Maya Lind" and quotation 2**
    - Supported. "skriver" correctly signals an email interview.
16. **Heading "Anteckningen tillskriver inte loggen den kortare tiden"**
    - Source: "does not attribute the difference to the software".
    - Supported. It does not turn assignment time into completion time.
17. **"31 felanmälningar", note dated 4 December 2025**
    - Supported.
18. **"Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före testet ingår inte i anteckningen."**
    - Source: "It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
    - Supported. The exclusion covers the whole note, so it also applies to the median figures.
19. **Median time report to assignment, 2 against 3 working days**
    - Supported.
20. **"Perioderna hade olika arbetsbelastning" and "avstår uttryckligen från att koppla skillnaden till programvaran"**
    - Source: "does not attribute".

    - Supported.
22. **"Hennes omdöme är inte en slutsats ur siffrorna …" and quotation 3**
    - Supported. The reservation survives inside the quotation.
23. **"Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger hon inte."**
    - Source: "did not recommend Svale to every housing company".
    - Supported.
24. **Heading "Större reparationer avgör fortsättningen"**
    - Source: "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs".
    - Differs: a timing condition becomes the deciding factor. **F7.**
25. **"Testet har ännu inte utvidgats till fler hus."**
    - Supported. It is narrower than the source and follows from it.
26. **"fattar sitt beslut när det har kontrollerat …"**
    - Supported.
27. **Checklist link**
    - Source: "a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial".
    - Supported.
28. **"publiceras av Svale Systems"**
    - Supported.

**Pronouns**
- **Lind:** every "hon" and "hennes" is third person singular. Feminine natural gender is supported by "Her final quotation is her actual … assessment".
- **The team:** "det" is grammatical neuter only and makes no natural-gender claim. It is singular, matching "It chose".
- **The log:** "den" is grammatical gender, singular.
- **Quotations:** "vi", "oss", "våra" and "jag" match "we", "us", "ours" and "I".

**Translated quotations**
- **Q1:** meaning, stance and voice are preserved.
- **Q2:** "innan nästa hus startar" keeps the same ellipsis as the English "before the next building starts", so it is not a defect.
- **Q3:** "samlad bild" is an idiomatic rendering of "one view", and the qualification is kept.

## B. Findings (source-support)

**F1. The title turns Lind's attributed judgement into the publisher's own claim and widens "us" to "Elm Quay".**
- A case where they part: Lind judges that the single view helps her team, but nothing measured shows a benefit to the company. The source says: "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."
- Repair: "Samlad bild hjälper underhållsteamet, säger arbetsledaren på Elm Quay".

**F2. The lede attributes the account of the figures to Lind.**
- The figures come from the internal note, and none of her quotations mentions them.
- Repair: "Arbetsledaren Maya Lind berättar vad teamet ville uppnå och hur hon skulle planera förberedelserna, och teamets interna testanteckning visar vad siffrorna visar och inte visar."

**F3 (minor). "vilken del av förberedelserna hon skulle ge mer tid" welds two remarks together.**
- A case where they part: she reserves the same amount of category time, planned in advance, and uses the extra week for preparation in general. Both quotations hold, yet no single part gets more time.
- Repair: "… och hur hon skulle planera tiden för förberedelserna inför nästa hus".

**F4 (minor). "emails" is narrowed to fault reports sent by email.**
- A case where they part: the emails were staff messages passed between shifts, not residents' reports. Nothing in the source rules this out.
- Repair: "Tidigare sparades telefonanmälningar och mejl var för sig."

**F5. The heading's "personalen" widens "six staff".**
- A case where they part: the team has more than six people. The source gives no team size.
- Repair: "Svale satte upp loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare".

**F6 (minor). "avstår … från att koppla" is stronger than "does not attribute".**
- A case where they part: the note records that the shorter time coincided with the trial, but attributes no cause.
- Repair: "anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden".

**F7. The heading makes larger repairs the deciding factor.**
- The source gives only a timing condition, and the team is the one that decides.
- Repair: "Teamet beslutar efter att ha prövat kategorierna på större reparationer".

## C. Translation findings

None.

## Completion status

Complete. F1–F7 are unresolved and remain open for the writer.

1	# Case-study brief and source
2	
3	SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.
4	
5	## Brief
6	
7	Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.
8	
9	## Material
10	
11	Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.
12	
13	The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.
14	
15	Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:
16	
17	- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
18	- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
19	- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”
20	
21	Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.
22	
23	## Forbidden inferences / judging
24	
25	No claim that software caused the shorter assignment time, saved money, delighted residents or rescued a helpless customer. Do not turn assignment time into completion time. The customer's reservation must survive. Judge whether quotations contribute experience beyond the surrounding narrative, whether supplier narration stays in third person and whether the suggested link accurately describes its destination.
26

1	# Samlad bild av felanmälningar hjälper, säger arbetsledaren
2	
3	Underhållsteamet på Elm Quay Housing prövade i åtta veckor en gemensam reparationslogg från Svale Systems i två hus. Arbetsledaren Maya Lind berättar vad teamet ville uppnå och hur hon skulle lägga upp förberedelserna en annan gång. En intern anteckning om testet redovisar siffrorna och deras begränsningar.
4	
5	Av Thomas Barregren
6	
7	Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter. Tidigare sparades telefonanmälningar och mejl var för sig. I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två av husen. Loggen i testet kom från Svale Systems, och om den ska användas i fler hus är ännu inte bestämt.
8	
9	## Statusvisningen prövades före valet
10	
11	Maya Lind är arbetsledare i underhållsteamet och har svarat på frågor via mejl. Hon beskriver vad teamet ville uppnå:
12	
13	– Vi ville att kvällspasset skulle se vad morgonpasset redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra, Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.
14	
15	Innan teamet valde Svale testade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje enskild reparation.
16	
17	## Svale stod för inställningar och utbildning
18	
19	Testet pågick i åtta veckor, och de boende kunde fortfarande felanmäla per telefon. Leverantören konfigurerade loggen och höll två utbildningstillfällen för sex medarbetare.
20	
21	Om arbetet med kategorierna skriver Maya Lind:
22	
23	– Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan nästa hus startar.
24	
25	## Anteckningen tillskriver inte loggen den kortare tiden
26	
27	Enligt Elm Quays interna testanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, fördes 31 felanmälningar in i loggen. Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställts före testet ingår inte i anteckningen.
28	
29	Under testet var mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning två arbetsdagar, jämfört med tre under de åtta veckorna innan. Perioderna hade olika arbetsbelastning, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte skillnaden till programvaran. Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller hur lång tid reparationerna tog att slutföra.
30	
31	## Maya Lind ser tillbaka på testet
32	
33	Hennes omdöme är inte en slutsats ur siffrorna utan hennes egen bedömning:
34	
35	– Jag skulle välja att göra testet igen. Att ha en samlad bild av anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle lägga in en extra vecka för förberedelser.
36	
37	Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger hon inte.
38	
39	## Kategorierna prövas på större reparationer före beslut
40	
41	Testet har ännu inte utvidgats till fler hus. Underhållsteamet fattar sitt beslut när det har kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer. Den som förbereder ett liknande införande kan läsa [checklistan för införandet](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist). Kundberättelsen publiceras av Svale Systems.
42

Underhållsteamet på Elm Quay Housing prövade i åtta veckor en gemensam reparationslogg från Svale Systems i två hus. Av Thomas Barregren

Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter. Tidigare sparades telefonanmälningar och mejl var för sig. I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två av husen. Loggen i testet kom från Svale Systems, och om den ska användas i fler hus är ännu inte bestämt.

## Statusvisningen prövades före valet

Maya Lind är arbetsledare i underhållsteamet och har svarat på frågor via mejl. Hon beskriver vad teamet ville uppnå:

Innan teamet valde Svale testade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje enskild reparation.

## Svale stod för inställningar och utbildning

Testet pågick i åtta veckor, och de boende kunde fortfarande felanmäla per telefon. Leverantören konfigurerade loggen och höll två utbildningstillfällen för sex medarbetare.

Om arbetet med kategorierna skriver Maya Lind:

– Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan nästa hus startar.

Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller hur lång tid reparationerna tog att slutföra.

– Jag skulle välja att göra testet igen. Att ha en samlad bild av anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle lägga in en extra vecka för förberedelser.
